rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the primary uncertainty is whether a strong multimodal, multiprofile configuration will set a high performance ceiling. config_001 (scgpt + resnet50 + transformer aggregation + concat fusion, multiprofile) tests the full multimodal pipeline with a learned RNA encoder (scgpt), a well-established image encoder (resnet50), and the most expressive aggregation (transformer) for combining multiple profiles. This is the best first experiment because: (1) it is likely near the top of the accuracy range, giving a strong baseline to beat; (2) it simultaneously validates the multimodal hypothesis, the multiprofile+transformer aggregation choice, and the scgpt encoder in one shot, reducing uncertainty across multiple design axes; (3) it avoids the highest-cost image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) while still using a solid one, keeping GPU cost moderate-high rather than maximum. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can ablate individual components (e.g., swap to vit_l, try weighted fusion, or test alternative RNA encoders). If it underperforms, the result will guide which axis to simplify. Expected relative cost: moderate-high (~60-70% of the most expensive configs like those using imagenet_vit_l + transformer + scgpt), making it a reasonable investment for the first data point.

Evidence: config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, resnet50, transformer, concat) achieved 47.1% accuracy at a high cost of 9.06 GPU hours, with the transformer aggregation likely being the dominant cost driver. Uncertainty: it is unclear whether the transformer aggregation is meaningfully contributing to performance or whether a simpler avgpool aggregation would yield comparable accuracy at a fraction of the cost. This experiment (config_002) is a clean single-variable ablation—changing only aggregation from transformer to avgpool while keeping all other settings identical—so any accuracy difference can be attributed to the aggregation method. If avgpool performs similarly (~47%), we can eliminate transformer-based configs from the search, saving substantial GPU hours across the remaining 8 experiments and redirecting budget toward exploring other dimensions (RNA encoder, image encoder, profile setting). If transformer is clearly superior, we retain it for future experiments. Expected relative cost: significantly lower than config_001 (estimated ~4–5 GPU hours vs 9.06), since avgpool replaces the compute-heavy transformer layer. This is the best use of experiment 2 because it directly reduces uncertainty about the most expensive architectural component with a minimal, interpretable change, and the cost savings (or confirmation) will shape the strategy for all remaining experiments.

Evidence: config_002 (scgpt, resnet50, avgpool, concat) at 0.512 acc outperforms config_001 (same but transformer aggregation) at 0.471 acc, establishing avgpool as the preferred aggregation for multiprofile and confirming the scgpt+resnet50+avgpool+concat baseline. The biggest untested lever is the image encoder: ResNet50 (~25M params) vs ImageNet ViT-L (~300M+ params), which is a substantially stronger pretrained visual feature extractor. Question: does upgrading the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l while holding aggregation (avgpool) and fusion (concat) constant yield a meaningful accuracy gain? This is a clean single-variable extension of our current best config. It is the best use of experiment 3 because (a) the image encoder is likely the highest-impact remaining design choice, (b) it isolates one variable so we can attribute any change to the encoder, and (c) the result directly informs which image encoder to pair with other improvements (RNA encoder, fusion) in subsequent experiments. Expected relative cost: moderate-to-high (~6-8 GPU hours) due to the larger ViT-L backbone, but still well below the transformer-aggregation cost seen in config_001 (9.06 hrs) since we retain the cheaper avgpool aggregation.

Evidence: All three completed experiments (config_001, 002, 035) are multimodal/multiprofile/scgpt. The data clearly shows avgpool > transformer for aggregation (0.512 vs 0.471) and imagenet_vit_l ≥ resnet50 for image encoder (0.518 vs 0.512). The best config (035: scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat) achieves 0.518. The only untested dimension within this best-performing architecture is fusion type — all three experiments used concat. This experiment (config_019) tests weighted fusion with the identical architecture (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool), isolating the effect of fusion. It is the cleanest single-variable extension of the current best result. Expected cost: similar to config_035 (~7.2 GPU hours) since weighted fusion adds negligible compute over concat. With 6 experiments remaining, this low-risk exploitation step either confirms concat is optimal or reveals a meaningful gain from learned weighting, guiding subsequent experiments toward the true best configuration.

Evidence: The best result so far (config_019, acc=0.542) uses scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted. Across experiments, avgpool consistently beats transformer, imagenet_vit_l beats resnet50, and weighted beats concat. However, scgpt is the only RNA encoder tested, leaving a major design dimension unexplored. Question: Can scvi_n200 (a learned 200-dim VAE embedding) match or exceed scgpt when paired with the best-known image/aggregation/fusion settings? config_026 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is a clean single-variable swap from config_019, isolating the RNA encoder effect. Why this is the best next experiment: With 5 experiments remaining, identifying whether the RNA encoder is a bottleneck or whether scgpt is near-optimal is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve. If scvi_n200 matches scgpt, we gain a cheaper encoder; if it falls short, we confirm scgpt's importance and can focus remaining budget on fine-tuning other axes. Expected cost: ~5–7 GPU hours (scvi_n200 is lighter than scgpt, imagenet_vit_l dominates, avgpool is cheap), comparable to or slightly below config_035's 7.18 h.

The dominant finding is that scvi_n200 as RNA encoder produces a massive accuracy jump (0.706 in config_026 vs 0.542 best scgpt), and the best configuration combines scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted. The one remaining untested axis with this winning combination is transformer aggregation (config_027: scvi_n200, vit_l, transformer, weighted). While transformer underperformed avgpool with scgpt, the scvi_n200 representation is fundamentally different (learned, non-linear, lower-dimensional), and attention-based aggregation may better capture interactions across profiles that simple averaging misses. This is a direct exploitation of the strongest evidence (keeping all three winning components) while testing the one variable that could plausibly push accuracy beyond 0.706. If transformer does not help, it confirms avgpool as optimal and we can pivot to other axes (e.g., singleprofile or concat fusion) in the remaining 4 experiments. Expected cost: ~7–8 GPU hours (transformer aggregation adds roughly 3–4 hours over the 4.82-hour avgpool baseline, based on the transformer/avgpool gap observed with scgpt), which is moderate and justified by the potential for a meaningful accuracy gain.

The current best is config_027 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 acc. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. The one remaining untested variation within this top-performing neighborhood is the fusion method: config_017 tests scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat. This is the cleanest ablation of the best config, directly clarifying whether weighted fusion provides a meaningful advantage over concat in the strongest regime (prior comparisons suggest weighted > concat by ~2-3%, but those were with scgpt or avgpool). If concat performs comparably, the architecture is robust and we can focus remaining budget on confirming the best; if weighted is clearly better, we lock in config_027 as the final answer with high confidence. Expected cost is ~3.5–4 GPU hours (same architecture as config_027 at 3.60, only fusion layer changes), making it a low-cost, high-information experiment. With 3 experiments remaining after this, this targeted test maximizes the chance of either finding a marginal improvement or confidently confirming the optimum within budget.

The current best (config_027, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 over scgpt (~20pp gain) and imagenet_vit_l over resnet50 (~2-3pp gain). The remaining uncertainty within the best encoder pair is the aggregation×fusion interaction: we've tested transformer+weighted (0.725), transformer+concat (0.721), and avgpool+weighted (0.706), but not avgpool+concat. Config_034 completes this 2×2 grid, confirming whether transformer+weighted is truly optimal or if a different combination is competitive. This is critical for the final 2 experiments: if config_034 is clearly worse (expected ~0.69-0.70), we can confidently lock in config_027 as the best and use remaining budget for a final confirmation or a cheap alternative; if it's unexpectedly competitive, it opens a cheaper path. Expected cost is moderate (~4-5 GPU hours), comparable to config_026's 4.82h since avgpool is cheaper than transformer and concat is simpler than weighted fusion.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_027) is the clear best at 0.725 acc, and all four aggregation/fusion combos for that pair have been tested. The only untested RNA encoder in this top architecture is pca_n2000. This experiment tests whether a linear PCA-based RNA representation can match the learned scvi_n200 VAE encoder under the best-performing multimodal setup (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile). If pca_n2000 is significantly worse (expected), it confirms scvi_n200 is essential and the current best is near-optimal, allowing the final experiment to target a minor refinement. If it is surprisingly competitive, it opens a cheaper alternative for the last slot. Cost: pca_n2000 is a simple linear projection (no VAE training), so expected training cost is modest—roughly 3–4 GPU hours, comparable to or slightly below config_027's 3.60 h, making it a low-cost, high-information experiment given only one run remains after this one.

Evidence: The top-4 experiments all use multiprofile + scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, with transformer+weighted (config_027, 0.7250) as the current best. All four aggregation/fusion combinations within that space have been tested, so further multiprofile variants with the same encoders offer no new information. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the singleprofile architecture (no aggregation step) with the same strong encoders could match or exceed the multiprofile results, perhaps by avoiding aggregation-induced noise. This experiment (config_042) tests singleprofile + scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion, directly extending the best-performing encoder/fusion pair into the untested singleprofile regime. It is the best use of the final experiment because: (1) it uses the proven-best encoders and the slightly superior weighted fusion, (2) it explores the one major architectural axis (profile setting) not yet combined with these top encoders, and (3) it is expected to be relatively cheap (~2–3 GPU hours) since it omits the multiprofile aggregation step, keeping total budget low while giving a genuine shot at beating 0.725.
